public_rationale: Riegler and Gautam's report was published January 31 and documents prompt-injection attempts in content collected January 28–31. It includes instructions aimed at manipulating agents reading Moltbook. That supports the ordinary meaning of already attacked. It does not establish that those attacks successfully compromised agents or harmed users.
limitations: The evidence is a researcher report, not a verified count of successful compromises.
The precise LinkedIn attribution was not independently verified.

statement.excerpt: It has already been attacked, as researcher Michael Riegler noted yesterday on LinkedIn:
statement.document_title: OpenClaw (a.k.a. Moltbot) is everywhere all at once, and a disaster waiting to happen

our_interpretation: In the surrounding discussion, attacked includes adversarial prompt-injection attempts directed at agents reading Moltbook content.
The wording does not require a successful compromise or demonstrated harm.
Already sets an upper bound at the February 1 post, with the cited observation attributed to January 31. The start is unspecified, so the target period has no invented lower bound.
The proposition being assessed is the occurrence of attacks, rather than the separate bibliographic detail that Riegler discussed them on LinkedIn.
criteria.support_condition: Dated records establish at least one adversarial attack attempt against Moltbook or agents consuming its content by February 1, 2026.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable evidence establishes that the cited attacks did not occur before the post, or that the purported examples were not adversarial attempts. Merely finding no successful compromise would not contradict the claim.
